answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks that later counterparties verify, with each accepted result unlocking a small stake-backed credential. A verifier who approves fabricated work risks losing its own stake when later evidence exposes the fraud, while a new identity must still pay the full deposit and build a track record. Splitting one attacker across many names therefore multiplies locked capital and verification costs rather than multiplying trusted influence; cedar, prism, and walnut can be task labels, not identities.
